summary: This Land was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which identified no deviation from the national position material enough to score separately (±0.02); it is therefore assessed at the national score. No Land-specific trans statute, enforcement series or event-security finding was located in the research pass; prison placement is Land competence and most other Länder have rewritten their placement rules in 2023-2026.

sources.summary: NOTE: page content did not load at fetch time (access denied); the underlying July 2026 report covers a convicted far-right extremist with a legally recognised female gender entry being transferred from a women's to a men's prison after public outcry - demonstrating that placement keys off the civil-registry entry and that contrary-placement exceptions are invoked inconsistently.

Constitutional-law blog essay (18 March 2026): most German Landers have quietly rewritten their prison-placement statutes since 2023 to accommodate legally recognised gender diversity (Rhineland-Palatinate's new provision took effect 1 March 2026, following Bavaria, Saxony and Hamburg), and analyses why tying placement to the registry sex entry - rather than the prisoner's own statement - raises constitutional problems for trans inmates; a legal-academic analysis, not Land-specific for this unit.

DW feature (23 August 2023): prisons are Land jurisdiction across Germany's 16 states; a transgender climate activist facing a possible sentence illustrated that men's prisons are inadequately prepared and understaffed to protect trans prisoners (some 2,000 prison-officer vacancies nationally; ~60,000 detainees across ~200 facilities); some states have built special accommodation or guidelines, but placement practice remains uneven.
